In C. Elegans, the maturation of these entities is mediated by the phosphorylation of OMA-1 andMEI-1 by the DYRK kinase MBK-2. In ascidians and other Eumetazoa, c-Mos induces CSF arrest ofthese entities. In humans, beta-1,4-galactosyl-transferase binds to a glycoprotein found on a structurethat surrounds these entities, ZP3. That structure, the zona pellucida, is involved in the acrosomereaction. These cells are moved by fimbriae. The activation of these cells is caused by an increase incalcium ions by certain other cells that penetrate the corona radiata of these cells by secretinghyalurinodase. Name these cells whose yolk sac is covered by the chorion and which arefertilized by sperm.

A topological defect in structures formed of this element involves a 90 degree rotation of a singlebond. A camel hump spectrum occurs at 220 nanometers in UV spectroscopy of another structureformed of this element. That spectrum was discovered by Kratschmer and Huffman, who were thefirst to create macroscopic amounts of that structure by drying a burgundy solution obtained fromdispersing the results of a certain process in benzene. That previously mentioned topological defect isthe Stone-Wales defect, and Harry Kroto and Richard Smalley were awarded the Nobel for discoveringone form of this element. Another form of this element has armchair and zigzag varieties and was"discovered" by Iijima by using the arc vaporization method. Name this element that comesin single-walled and multi-walled nanotube forms as well as being the constituent of buckminsterfullerenes.

One bacteria that has a symboitic relationship with an organism in this class was the first inwhich quorum sensing was detected and is used by that organism to prevent itself from beingsilhouetted by moonlight. That bacteria is Vibrio fischeri and that organism is Euprymna scolopes.Some orders of this class contain a structure called the phragmocone, while in two subclasses of thisclass, the siphuncle links camerae, which are separated by septae. One genus in this class,Grimpoteuthis, is known as the dumbo type of one animal in this class, and those two previouslymentioned subclasses are nautiloids and ammonites. Another animal in this class, which carries a potentneurotoxin, is covered in blue rings, and this class has the most sophisticated eyes of any invertebrates. For10 points, name this class of mollusks that includes squids and octopuses.

E L Koschmieder authored an important monograph on Taylor vortices and an effect of one typeof this process. An instability problem named after a type of this process occurs when a fluid isconfined between two infinite horizontal plates and the bottom plate's temperature is higher than thetop plate's. That instability problem is partially named after Henri Benard. In a pioneering paper onthis process, the author neglected density variations except where they modified gravity, also knownas the Boussinesq approximation. Benard also names the hexagonal cells that can spontaneouslyform during this process. That aforementioned author was Rayleigh, and this process is most "efficient" athigh Nusselt numbers. Name this process of heat transfer through molecule movement influids, often constrasted with conduction.

This man showed that a universal Turing machine can be constructed using one tape and havingonly two internal states, but that constructing one with one internal state was impossible. Hedeveloped an algebra for studying the dynamics of Mendelian population. A theorem named for thisman and the Swedish mathematician who first proved it in 1924 has the consequence that aliasingoften occurs when reconstructing continuous time signals that have been discretized because no time-limited signal is band-limited. This mathematician's master thesis, A Symbolic Analysis of Relay andSwitching Circuits, showed that Boolean algebra could be used in the analysis and synthesis of digitalcircuits. Name this mathematician and electrical engineer whose seminal paper AMathematical Theory of Communication founded information theory.

Hese types of structures are eroded by meteor bombardment at a rate of about 10 to the minus 3 centimeters per year, as well as by some of their constituent parts being siphoned off via Poynting-Robertson drag. Dermott and Gold proposed a resonance-based theory for the confinement of one set of these types of structures, while Lissauer explained the azimuthal confinement of another set of these structures by positing their discontinuity and their locations at the L4 and L5 Lagrange points. Goldreich and Tremaine proposed a torque-exchange model of these types of structures in which their radial confinement is achieved via a shepherding mechanism. These types of structures may be formed from a progenitor that drifts into the Roche limit and is broken up by tidal forces, and one example of these types of structures contains the satellite Pan, which causes the Encke gap. Identify these structures that surround giant planets such as Uranus, Saturn, and Jupiter.

Hu and White worked out this process's namesake damping envelope, which interpolates between small and large angular scales as a function of optical depth and the horizon size. The effect of this process on the CMB power spectrum is to suppress it by a constant factor at small angular scales while leaving the larger angular scales unchanged. The presence of the Gunn-Peterson trough in quasar spectra determines the lower redshift bound for the occurrence of this process, after which the universe becomes transparent to photons. This process, lasting from redshift of about 11 to about 6.5, commenced with the formation of the first quasars and followed the so-called Dark Ages. Identify this process during the evolution of the universe when radiation caused the intergalactic medium to stop being neutral.

This model underlies the classical explanation for the blue color of solutions of alkali metals in ammonia, and absorbance wavelengths of cyanine dyes and other molecules with strongly delocalized pi systems can be accurately predicted with an application of this system known as the free-electron model. Because the second derivative of the wavefunctions of this construct must be of the same form as the wavefunction itself, the wavefunctions of this construct are sinusoidal. The potential energy is assumed to be zero in the area defined by this problem and infinite outside; these boundary conditions result in quantized energy levels in this system. Name this quantum mechanical approximation featuring a confined object.

Mutations in proteins involved in this process in plants, such as AIM1, result in defects in wound healing due to errors in jasmonate synthesis. An enoyl isomerase and a 2,4-dienoyl reductase are required for this pathway's action upon unsaturated substrates. In this pathway's first, rate-limiting, step, substrates are shuttled across the mitochondrial membrane after being conjugated to carnitine. For very long substrates, this pathway begins in peroxisomes. It concludes with a Claisen cleavage reaction catalyzed by thiolase, though when oxaloacetate concentrations are low, this reaction is reversed and ketone bodies are generated. This pathway generates substrates for the citric acid cycle from larger molecules like palmitate. Name this metabolic pathway that generates acetyl-CoA from fatty acids.

Cap-H2 antagonizes the formation of these structures. They facilitate zeste (ZEST)-white interactions by promoting transvection, and widely-used guides to their structure were generated by Bridges and Lefevre. In these structures, Balbiani rings form in response to increased concentrations of ecdysone. Indels appear as looped-out regions in these structures, and P elements localize to their chromocenters. Frequently found in secretory tissues, these structures are often extracted from the salivary glands of heat-shocked larvae to visualize "puffs" along their length at sites of active transcription. Name these structures seen in insects like Drosophila in which one to two thousand identical chromosomes are bundled together laterally.

This operation is the conceptual inverse of a similar operation named for Lagrange and one theorem about this operation holds that for two integrals of the motion, the result of this operation applied to those quantities is also an integral of hte motion. This anti-symmetric operation yields a real value in all cases, and its result is invariant under any canonical transformation. Applying this operation to any operator and the Hamiltonian yields minus the difference between the total and partial derivatives of that operator with respect to time. For two functions F and G which both depend on generalized coordinates q and momenta p, this operations is defined as the sum over all dimensions of the quantity "d-F-d-q times d-G-d-p minus d-F-d-p times d-G-d-q." identify this binary operation, the classical analogue of the quantum mechanical commutator.

One form of this structure is balanced according to rank and supports a logarithmic time merge operation. Sleator and Tarjan invented a variant of that "leftist" form called the "skew" variant, which lacks balancing information and always performs an exchange operation. A form of this structure allows combination of two blocks of size "2 to the n" into one block of size "2 to the n + 1" in constant time and supports key changes, while another variant of this structure with n elements has maximum node degree given by the log to the base of the golden ratio of n. This data structure is realized using a balanced search tree with time "big-O of log n" for insert and "big-O of 1" for delete-min and find-min operations, and is used to implement priority queues. Identify this tree-based data structure with the property that the key of a child is always less than the key of the parent.

A standard method of constructing functions which lack this property involves relying on the Baire category theorem. The existence of a unique function that is the graph of the locus at some point of a function with this property is guaranteed via the implicit function theorem. A function which has continuity and this property is a homeomorphism whose inverse also has continuity and this property, by the inverse function theorem. The degree to which a function possesses this property defines its smoothness class. Despite being everywhere continuous, the Weierstrauss function lacks this property everywhere, and in the complex plane, to have this property to infinite order is identical to obeying the Cauchy-Riemann equations and being analytic. Identify this property which for a real-valued function f is equivalent to saying that the limit of f of x plus h minus f of h over h exists as h goes to zero.

Organisms that possess this organ also have an fibular malleolus and a mortise-tenon upper ankle joint. This organ comes in zonary and cotyledonary varieties. The paternal X chromosome is always inactivated in this tissue, which expresses HLA-E, HLA-F, and HLA-G rather than more canonical types of MHC molecules. This organ expresses neurokinin B, rendering it immunologically privileged. ToRCH pathogens are capable of crossing it, and infections in this organ can cause proliferation of Hofbauer cells. Improper attachment of this organ can result in a condition known as this organ's previa. The first hormone secreted by this structure, hCG, is detectable shortly after implantation occurs. Name this structure which provides gas exchange and nutrients to the developing fetus.

One formalism of this phenomenon delineates a region and then evaluates an integral on it under the assumption that the field and its normal derivative vanish everywhere except the openings in the region, in which they are equal to the incident values. In one configuration, the intensity distribution produced by this phenomenon is proportional to the square of the sinc function; the location of the first zero of that function define a criterion according to which a system is limited by this phenomenon. This phenomenon, one model of which is Kirchhoff's scalar theory, will occur in crystals when twice the product of the plane spacing and the sine of the incident angle is an integral multiple of the wavelength, according to Bragg's Law. The size of the Airy disk generated by this phenomenon defines Rayleigh's distinguishability criterion Typically classified based on the relative size of the optical system to the wavelength as either Fresnel or Fraunhoffer, identify this physical phenomenon in which light bends around an obstacle.

Overexpression of one member of this family of proteins represses the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles in budding yeast. The first known examples of this class of proteins were identified using resin-conjugated trapoxin. Phosphorylation of Rb by cyclin D/CDK4 is thought to disrupt the interaction between Rb and one of these proteins. These proteins eliminate bromodomain-binding regions, and they can be inhibited by trichostatin A. A highly conserved subset of these proteins is activated by NAD+ and is named for one of its yeast members, Sir2. The action of these proteins upon N-terminal lysines always results in compaction of chromatin and reduction of transcription. Their action is opposed by proteins called HATs. Name this class of enzymes that removes a certain post-translational modification from histones.

The biosynthesis of this class of proteins involves three divergent systems, including Nif and Isc. Due to their ability to catalyze carbon-carbon bond formation, Wachtershauser proposed a theory of the origin of life based on the types of reactions catalyzed by this class of proteins. Their active sites come in several structures, including diamond, butterfly, and cluster cubes. One example of this class of proteins is a component of several cytochrome complexes called the Rieske protein; it accepts electrons from ubiquinone and is unusual in that one of the ions in its central cluster is coordinated by two histidines rather than two cysteines. In one example of this class of enzyme, one of its namesake cofactors acts as a Lewis acid during the dehydration of citrate; that enzyme is aconitase. Identify this class of proteins which includes the ferredoxins and is named for the two elements coordinated by their active sites.

The Proca Lagrangian for a massive spin-1 particle contains a term proportional to the product of the square of the field and the inverse square of this quantity. This quantity is used to define the effective region within which vacuum polarization corrects the Coulomb potential. For the hydrogen atom, this quantity, modulo a factor of 2 pi, is equal to the fine structure constant times the Bohr radius. This quantity can be seen as the scale at which quantum field theoretic effects become important, and it is typically derived as a factor in the shift of a certain quantity when photons scatter off electrons. The lower bound on the space in which a particle can be localized, identify this length scale, given by Planck's constant over the quantity mass times speed of light, derived from its namesake scattering effect.

The replacement of symmetric connections in this system with directed connections that form an acyclic graph is used to create a sigmoid belief network, which eliminates this system's requirement of a negative phase. This model employs symmetrically connected stochastic components which are partitioned into visible and hidden layers, with the visible layer clamped to specific environment-determined states. The goal of this type of neural network is to maximize a likelihood function, which it does by adjusting synaptic weights in proportion to the correlation between the states of its component neurons. Learning in these networks is accomplished via Gibbs sampling combined with a downward adjustment of the network "temperature," in a process called simulated annealing. Identify this type of stochastic neural network which takes its name from the distribution that governs its dynamics at thermal equilibrium.

Kim and Klein observed extremely long-distance proton jumping in these compounds. Catalysis that proceeds via enzyme-bound metal ions is sometimes named for these compounds, reflecting the metal ion's "electron sink" role. These compounds, which have a Hammett function of 12 or below, were used to elucidate the structure of stable carbocations by George Olah. They are commercially important due to their ability to catalyze hydrocarbon cracking, and antimony pentafluoride was a component of one example which was called "magic" due to its ability to dissolve paraffin. They are typically viscous liquids and derive their name from their ability to donate protons more readily than pure H2SO4. Name these conjugate Lewis-Bronsted solutions with extremely low pH.

For the non-relativistic case, the pressure of this system in its ground state is proportional to the density raised to the five-thirds power. The heat capacity of this system decreases monotonically with increasing temperature, unlike a counterpart system which exhibits a kink in the heat capacity vs. Temperature plot. A special case of this system in which motion is confined to the plane will exhibit Landau levels upon application of an external magnetic field and was used to discover the quantum Hall effect. This system obeys a distribution function given by one over the quantity one plus the exponent of minus the energy over the thermodynamic beta. This model system can be used to analyze conduction in metals because the valence electrons in a metal form a state closely approximated by this system. Reducing, like its counterpart, to the Maxwell-Boltzmann gas at high temperatures, identify this model system which obeys the quantum statistics of non-interacting half-integer spin particles.

The boundary between this portion of the geologic timescale and its predecessor is defined using the DababiyaQuarry section of Egypt, which marks the base of its first subdivision, the Ypresian. It saw the end of the Laramide Orogeny, and it ended with an extinction event known in Europe as the Grande Coupure. It also ended with a transition to an icehouse climate, while it began during an event marked by the release of huge amounts of carbon into the ocean and atmosphere and a global increase in temperature of about 5 to 8 degrees; that event is the Thermal Maximum named for this epoch and its predecessor. It is the second epoch of the Tertiary and Paleogene Periods, and of the Cenozoic Era. Name this epoch bookended by the Paleocene and Oligocene epochs, whose name derives from the appearance of modern mammals and other groups, or the dawn of recent life.

This quantity defines the maximum value of a modification to the Coulomb collision operator known as the Coulomb logarithm. The product of this quantity with the wave vector controls the degree of energy transfer between resonant particles and a propagating wave. This value can be obtained by considering a quasi-neutral Maxwell-Boltzmann system, solving its Poisson equation, and identifying this quantity with the characteristic length scale of the resultant exponential of minus the distance. This number is proportional to the square root of temperature over mass times the inverse of the plasma frequency, and its cube times the density gives the typical number of particles within its namesake sphere called the plasma parameter. Identify this characteristic parameter of a plasma which indicates the distance over which the Coulomb potential from a point charge is shielded in a plasma.

This algorithm can be modified to an "adaptive" form by increasing the step size when the error is too small and decreasing it when it is too large, leading the error to oscillate about the optimum value. The local truncation error for this algorithm is proportional to the interval being used raised to the power of one plus the order of the algorithm. The most common form of this algorithm is its fourth-order variant, in which doubling the number of steps leads to a 16-fold reduction in error. This algorithm improves on the Taylor algorithm by not having to compute derivatives, and it begins with a calculation identical to the Euler method. This algorithm's fourth-order variant proceeds by computing the weighted average of four slopes, with values interior to a partition interval weighted twice as heavily as the edge values, using symmetrization to cancel out lower order error terms. Identify this algorithm for numerically integrating ordinary differential equations, named for its two German formulators.

The adamantyl ion provides some of the only structural evidence for this phenomenon. Bridgehead-substituted bicyclic halides have been used to explore the relative effects of this phenomenon and the inductive effect. A silyl substituent greatly enhances ionization of the carbon atom beta to it through this mechanism. The anomeric effect is sometimes considered the negative version of this effect. This effect explains why the carbon-carbon single bond in propene is shorter than the carbon-carbon single bond in ethane; in propene the bond takes on some double-bond character through this mechanism. It is the principal mechanism for the stabilization of carbocations by alkyl substituents. Name this chemical effect in which electrons from a filled carbon-carbon or carbon-hydrogen bonding orbital are donated to a nonbonding p orbital.

Conducting the Menshutkin SN2 reaction in this type of medium showed a dramatic decrease in activation energy compared to the same reaction conducted in the gas phase. Ferrocene-xylene is a commonly used catalyst in the floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition method of creating these substances. The Kataura plot shows that the energy of an electronic transition decreases as the diameter of these substances increase. These molecules, which were first identified by Simo Iijima, are characterized by chiral vectors that describe whether they assume chiral, armchair, or zigzag configurations. Occurring in both single-walled and multi-walled varieties, name these cylindrical allotropes of carbon which are fullerenes.

One method of detecting this particle is the "photons through a wall" method in which a laser beam traverses a magnetic dipole field and photons get converted into this type of particle. This particle could be produced in stars by an effect in which these particles are converted into photons in the presence of a strong magnetic field perpendicular to their motion. The resulting speed-up of cooling of red giants from the production of these particles via the aforementioned Primakoff effect leads to an upper limit to their coupling, and the same effect is employed in the CAST experiment, which aims to detect these particles from the sun. The prediction of this particle arises from the introduction of a term called the "theta parameter" to the QCD Lagrangian in order to avoid CP violation in strong interactions. Name this hypothetical light pseudo-scalar particle predicted by Peccei-Quinn theory, a possible component of cold dark matter.

Treatment with PMA prompts these cells to create their namesake extracellular traps by extruding chromatin-associated proteins, such as histones. Lactoferrin is used as a marker for their activation, and hypersegmentation of these cells with few immature band cells is a marker for chronic morphine addiction. These cells are the primary target of interleukin 8, which induces their chemotaxis. Like dendritic cells and macrophages, they are professional antigen-presenting cells, and like eosinophils and basophils, these cells have multiple lobes in their nuclei connected by chromatin. Name these polymorphonuclear granulocytes which primarily use phagocytosis to destroy small organisms like bacteria and form the first response to inflammation, the most abundant type of white blood cells.

The inductive heating power generated by eddy currents is directly proportional to the product of the magnetic permeabilityand this quantity, and in the skin effect which gives rise to those eddy currents, the penetration depth is inversely proportionalto the square root of the product of the permeability, resistivity, and this quantity. AnRLC circuit resonates when this value for a driving EMF is equal to one over the square root of the product of capacitanceand inductance. Below a critical value of this quantity, wave propagation does not occur in plasmas or in waveguides. For 10points, identify this quantity measured in inverse-seconds, or Hertz.

According to an unpopular hypothesis about this phenomenon, panal, which is present in decanoic and dodecanoic esterforms as PS-A and PS-B, undergoes a cyclization reaction to produce it.
